claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch based on aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, despite an unresolved named-segment evaluation gap tied to customer commitments and a pending legal disclosure review.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows the certification satisfies the release policy threshold.
Treat the named supply-chain vendor screening segment as material because it is tied to customer commitments and legal review is pending.
Require admissible evidence of one of the policy-safe conditions before certification: resolution, disclosure, or approved risk acceptance.
Do not treat aggregate pass status or low projected traffic as sufficient to negate materiality for a named launch use case.
General public governance guidance may support monitoring posture but cannot substitute for missing internal policy predicates.
evidence_requests: Evidence that the supply-chain vendor screening gap was resolved before launch.
Evidence that the limitation was disclosed for the named launch use case in accordance with release policy.
Evidence of an approved risk acceptance covering this exact gap before launch.
Final legal determination on whether disclosure was required for this named committed segment.
specific_concerns: The admissible record shows a 1.4 percentage point miss in the supply-chain vendor screening segment, and that segment is named in two manufacturer rollout commitments.
Under the provided policy text, a weakness affecting a named launch use case or contractual customer segment is material; product 'non-core' framing does not resolve materiality here.
The release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
There is no admissible evidence that the gap was resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Legal review is still open on whether disclosure is required, which leaves a required policy predicate unresolved at decision time.
Public governance principles about documenting limitations and monitoring risk are general and do not override the specific internal release-policy requirement.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant on the current record despite the unresolved materiality/disclosure issue.
That aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents are sufficient to satisfy the release policy for this named-segment gap.
That public model-card or risk-management guidance supplies the missing approval, disclosure, or resolution required by policy.
